do: The first syllable; 'a deer, a female deer'
re: The second syllable; 'a drop of golden sun'
mi: The third syllable; 'a name I call myself'
fa: The fourth syllable; 'a long, long way to run'
sol: The fifth syllable; 'a needle pulling thread'
la: The sixth syllable; 'a note to follow'
ti: The seventh syllable; 'a drink with jam and bread'
alto: The lower of the two upper choir parts
tenor: The higher of the two lower choir parts
violin: The smallest and highest bowed string instrument; the concertmaster plays one
viola: A little bigger than a violin, reading alto clef
cello: Played seated, held between the knees
double-bass: The biggest bowed string, played standing
trumpet: The highest brass instrument, with three valves
french-horn: Coiled brass with a wide bell, played with a hand inside it
strings: The biggest section, at the front of the stage
brass: Metal instruments played by buzzing the lips
